description: Verify that DUT does NOT emit ICMP Parameter Problem for a datagram whose destination is an IP broadcast, even when its options are malformed — broadcast destinations must not generate per-host error replies (RFC 1122 §3.2.2 SHOULD NOT)
approach:
[Objective]
If every host on a broadcast segment replied to a malformed broadcast packet with an ICMP error, the sender would be flooded. RFC 1122 §3.2.2 forbids generating ICMP error messages in response to datagrams sent to broadcast or multicast destinations.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 datagram
   • dst_ip      = broadcast (e.g. 255.255.255.255 or subnet broadcast)
   • IP options  = malformed Internet Timestamp

2. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no ICMP Parameter Problem

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ICMP Parameter Problem within the window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT emitted Parameter Problem despite the broadcast destination. Indicates the broadcast-suppression rule is missing.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the malformed broadcast — normal RFC 1122 §3.2.2 behaviour
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT emitted Parameter Problem for a broadcast datagram — flood risk
